english: to stare at / look up at
usage: 빤히 is the most natural adverb partner — a direct, unblinking stare
멍하니 adds a vacant, zoned-out quality
힐끔 softens it to a quick stolen look rather than a long stare
to look up at the ceiling
Shows the literal 'look upward' nuance baked into 쳐다-
examples: 고양이가 저를 쳐다봐요
The cat is looking at me
Simple present; subject + 를 + 쳐다보다 is the basic frame
모르는 사람이 저를 계속 쳐다봐서 좀 불편했어요
A stranger kept staring at me, so I felt a bit uncomfortable
계속 + 쳐다보다 brings out the unwelcome lingering-gaze tone
다들 휴대폰만 쳐다보고 있어요
Everyone is just glued to their phones
휴대폰만 쳐다보다 = eyes locked on the screen; -고 있다 marks the ongoing state
nuance: 쳐다보다 is built from 치어다(보다) ('look upward') fused with 보다, and that upward/fixed feel survives: it means to look directly and steadily at something, frequently raising your eyes (천장을, 하늘을 쳐다보다). The dividing line from plain 보다 is intensity and duration — 보다 is any neutral 'see/look', while 쳐다보다 is a held, pointed gaze. Against 바라보다 (a calm, fond, distant gaze) it is far less warm: aimed at a person it slides easily into the uncomfortable 'why are you staring at me' zone, so 왜 쳐다봐요? sounds mildly confrontational. It conjugates as a 보다-verb: 보 + -아 contracts to 봐, giving 쳐다봐요 / past 쳐다봤어요. English-speaker pitfall: don't reach for 쳐다보다 every time you'd say 'look at' — for watching TV, a movie, or a performance you want 보다, and forcing 쳐다보다 there sounds like you're glaring at the screen.

structuredNuance.t: To look directly and steadily at something, frequently raising your eyes (천장을, 하늘을 쳐다보다). It is a held, pointed gaze rather than a neutral look.

Marking the target with 에 instead of 를. It's 저를 쳐다봐요, not 저에 쳐다봐요 — 쳐다보다 takes a direct object with 을/를.

usage: to look in the same direction
Often figurative: sharing the same goals/values
to gaze at the distant mountains
Highlights the 'at a distance' feel of the word
examples: 하늘을 바라봤어요
I gazed at the sky
Basic past form; calm, contemplative single look
퇴근길에 한강을 바라보면 마음이 편해져요
Gazing at the Han River on the way home calms me down
-면 conditional + 바라보다 = a soothing habitual scene
우리는 같은 곳을 바라보고 있어요
We are looking in the same direction
Figurative use about shared values; -고 있다 for an ongoing stance
nuance: 바라보다 (from 바라- + 보다) is to look at something usually at some distance and with a calm, often emotional or contemplative feeling — scenery, a loved one's face, the future. The key contrast is with 쳐다보다: where 쳐다보다 is a pointed, sometimes prickly stare, 바라보다 is soft and almost never aggressive, which makes it the safe verb for looking fondly or wistfully at someone (사랑스럽게 바라보다). Against 보다 (any plain 'see/look'), 바라보다 adds emotional depth and the sense of holding your eyes on something across space. It also lives a second, figurative life — 같은 곳을 바라보다, 미래를 바라보다 — meaning to share a vision or face the future. It conjugates as a regular 보다-verb: 바라보 + -아 → 바라봐요, past 바라봤어요. English-speaker pitfall: don't use 바라보다 for reading fine print or inspecting an object up close; that nearness belongs to 살펴보다 or 보다, since 바라보다 implies looking across a gap, not scrutinizing.

mistakes: Using 바라보다 for reading small text or inspecting something up close. 계약서를 바라봤어요 sounds like you admired it from afar; for checking details say 살펴봤어요.
Confusing it with the homophone-feel of 바라다 ('to wish/hope'). 바라보다 (gaze) and 바라다 (hope) are different verbs — 행복을 바라요 = I wish for happiness, not 바라봐요.
Adding an aggressive adverb like 노려보듯 to 바라보다. The word's whole point is its gentle tone; pairing it with hostility contradicts it — use 노려보다 for an angry stare.

usage: 꼼꼼히 is the signature adverb for careful checking
Common in safety advice before crossing or acting
Reviewing a document line by line
examples: 메뉴를 좀 살펴볼게요
Let me look over the menu for a moment
Polite -ㄹ게요 to a server; calm, attentive checking
집을 계약하기 전에 옵션을 꼼꼼히 살펴보세요
Before signing for the place, examine the options carefully
꼼꼼히 살펴보다 in a practical housing context
증상을 좀 더 살펴보고 약을 드릴게요
Let me examine your symptoms a bit more, then give you medicine
Pharmacy/clinic register; -고 chains observe-then-act
nuance: 살펴보다 joins 살피다 ('to scan/watch attentively, take care') with 보다, so its core is attentive, careful looking — to review, inspect, or check something over until you understand it: documents, a room, symptoms, your surroundings. It is the everyday 'review/check over' verb and pairs habitually with 꼼꼼히 ('meticulously'). The sharp contrast is with 둘러보다: 둘러보다 is a relaxed sweep around a whole space, while 살펴보다 zooms in with intent to verify, so 가게를 둘러봤어요 (browsed the shop) and 가게를 살펴봤어요 (inspected/cased the shop) feel quite different. Versus 훑어보다 (a fast skim for the gist), 살펴보다 is slower and more thorough. As a 보다-verb it contracts 살펴보 + -아 → 살펴봐요, past 살펴봤어요. English-speaker pitfall: 'look over' in English can mean both 'skim' and 'scrutinize', but 살펴보다 only covers the careful end — if you mean a quick glance, use 훑어보다, not 살펴보다.

Dropping the object particle in set advice. It's 주변을 살펴보세요, not 주변 살펴보세요 in careful speech — 살펴보다 governs a 을/를 object.

usage: to look into how to do something
The 'investigate/research' sense; super common life-admin phrase
Negative with 못 — couldn't recognize someone/something
examples: 제가 한번 알아볼게요
I'll look into it
The go-to work/service line; -ㄹ게요 promises to check on it
가격을 여기저기 알아보고 제일 싼 데서 샀어요
I checked prices here and there and bought from the cheapest place
여기저기 알아보다 = shop around; -고 chains research-then-buy
머리를 자르니까 친구가 저를 못 알아봤어요
After I got a haircut my friend didn't recognize me
Recognition sense with 못; -니까 gives the cause
nuance: 알아보다 fuses 알다 ('know') with 보다, and the two senses both fall out of 'look in order to know.' Sense 1 — investigate / look into / research (information, prices, options, procedures): 비자 연장 방법을 알아보다. This is one of the most useful verbs for living in Korea — 제가 알아볼게요 is how you tell someone you'll check on a matter. Sense 2 — recognize / make out (a face, handwriting, a thing): 글씨를 못 알아보겠어요. The crucial contrast is with plain 알다: 알다 is the static state 'to know', while 알아보다 is the active 'find out' or 'identify on sight' — you can 알다 a fact, but you 알아보다 to obtain it. It contracts as 알아보 + -아 → 알아봐요, past 알아봤어요; the recognition sense often appears negative as 못 알아보다. English-speaker pitfall: for 'recognize someone' don't use 알다 — 그 사람을 알아요 means you know them, while 그 사람을 알아봤어요 means you recognized them by sight.

Saying 찾다 when you mean to research options. 찾다 is 'to search for/find', but 'I'll look into it (and weigh the choices)' is 알아볼게요, not 찾을게요.

english: to watch over / keep an eye on
usage: to wait and see a bit longer
The classic 'let's monitor before deciding' phrase
보조동사 -아 주다 adds a caring, protective nuance
examples: 제가 가방 좀 지켜볼게요
I'll keep an eye on the bag
Everyday favor; -ㄹ게요 offers to watch it
상태가 어떤지 며칠 더 지켜봅시다
Let's watch the condition for a few more days
-읍시다 doctor's 'let's monitor it'; classic wait-and-see
환율을 며칠 지켜보다가 환전할 거예요
I'll watch the exchange rate a few days, then exchange money
-다가 marks watching that leads into a later action
nuance: 지켜보다 combines 지키다 ('to guard/keep') with 보다, so unlike a one-off look it means to watch continuously over time — to monitor, keep an eye on, or 'wait and see.' That 지키다 root gives it a flavor of care or guardianship, which is why it dominates medical advice (며칠 더 지켜봅시다 = let's observe a few more days), parenting (아이를 지켜보다), and decisions you want to postpone until things develop (상황을 지켜보다). Contrast it with 쳐다보다 and 바라보다, which are momentary looks: 지켜보다 is durative — you keep looking across a stretch of time. It also differs from 살펴보다, which is a careful inspection at one moment rather than ongoing surveillance. With the helper -아 주다 it becomes warmly protective: 지켜봐 주다 = watch over someone for their sake. It contracts 지켜보 + -아 → 지켜봐요, past 지켜봤어요. English-speaker pitfall: don't use 지켜보다 for watching a show or game for fun — that single sitting is 보다; 지켜보다 implies vigilant, time-extended monitoring.

Treating it as a quick glance. 지켜보다 is durative; for an instant look use 쳐다보다 or 보다. 한 번 지켜봤어요 sounds odd because the verb implies sustained watching.

usage: to just browse / just look around
The exact phrase for telling a clerk you're only browsing
to take a look around (one loop)
한 바퀴 = one round/circuit of a place
to look around at one's leisure
What staff say: take your time browsing
examples: 그냥 둘러보는 거예요
I'm just browsing
The set reply to '도와드릴까요?'; -는 거예요 states what you're doing
사기 전에 매장을 한 바퀴 둘러봤어요
I looked around the store once before buying
한 바퀴 둘러보다 = do a full loop of the place
새 동네로 이사 와서 주변을 둘러보고 있어요
I moved to a new neighborhood, so I'm looking around the area
-고 있다 for the ongoing exploring
nuance: 둘러보다 is built from 두르다/둘러- ('to encircle, go around') plus 보다, so it literally means to send your eyes around a whole space — a store, a neighborhood, an exhibition — taking a broad, relaxed look. It is the natural verb for browsing: when a clerk asks 도와드릴까요?, the textbook reply is 그냥 둘러볼게요 or 둘러보는 거예요 ('I'm just looking'). The decisive contrast is with 들여다보다, its near-opposite: 둘러보다 is a wide sweep over many things, while 들여다보다 is a close peer into one thing, so 가게를 둘러보다 (browse the shop) vs 가방을 들여다보다 (peer into the bag). It also contrasts with 살펴보다, which adds careful scrutiny rather than a casual survey. As a 보다-verb it contracts 둘러보 + -아 → 둘러봐요, past 둘러봤어요. English-speaker pitfall: don't use 둘러보다 for inspecting a single item closely — surveying a whole space is its job; for examining one thing carefully, switch to 살펴보다.

english: to peer into / look closely at
usage: Looking into an enclosed or small space
to peer down at one's phone
Bending over a screen with focused attention
to look closely into a problem
Figurative: examine an issue in depth
to pore over for a long while
examples: 아이가 어항을 들여다봐요
The child is peering into the fish tank
Simple present; leaning in toward a small space
문제가 뭔지 제가 한번 들여다볼게요
Let me take a close look at what the problem is
Figurative 'examine in detail'; -ㄹ게요 offers to dig in
서류를 한참 들여다봤는데도 이해가 안 됐어요
Even after poring over the document a while, I didn't get it
한참 들여다보다 = study intently; -는데도 = even though
nuance: 들여다보다 comes from 들이다 ('to bring/let inward') in the -여다 form plus 보다 — literally 'look inward into' — so it means a close, leaning-in look into something: a container, a screen, or, figuratively, a problem. The defining feature is up-close, focused attention, usually with your head bent toward the object. The sharp contrast is with 둘러보다: 들여다보다 narrows onto one thing from near, while 둘러보다 sweeps broadly over a space — peering into a bag vs scanning a whole store. Against 살펴보다 (careful inspection that can be at normal distance), 들여다보다 adds the physical sense of bringing your eyes right up to or inside something. Figuratively, 문제를 들여다보다 means to examine an issue in depth, much like English 'look into.' It contracts 들여다보 + -아 → 들여다봐요, past 들여다봤어요. English-speaker pitfall: don't swap it with 둘러보다 — a close look into one thing is 들여다보다, a broad look around a space is 둘러보다.

usage: to peek at someone else's things
to peek through a crack in the door
Idiomatic: bide your time, look for an opening
Neutral figurative: something offers a glimpse into
examples: 남의 휴대폰을 엿보면 안 돼요
You shouldn't peek at someone else's phone
-면 안 되다 = it's not allowed; clear improper nuance
옆 사람 답안지를 엿보면 부정행위예요
Peeking at the next person's answer sheet is cheating
Exam context; squarely negative
이 책에서는 조선시대 생활을 엿볼 수 있어요
This book lets you glimpse life in the Joseon era
Figurative 'offers a glimpse'; perfectly neutral here
nuance: 엿보다 uses the prefix 엿- ('secretly, on the sly') plus 보다, so its base meaning is to look at something furtively — peeking through a gap, spying, or sneaking a look at someone's private things. In its literal sense it almost always sounds sneaky or improper (남의 일기를 엿보다 = snoop in someone's diary), which sets it firmly apart from open looking verbs like 보다 or 바라보다. Two idiomatic extensions soften or neutralize it, though: 기회를 엿보다 ('watch for an opening', a normal strategic phrase) and ~을 엿볼 수 있다 ('offers a glimpse into', common in writing about an era, a culture, or someone's inner world). It contracts 엿보 + -아 → 엿봐요, past 엿봤어요. English-speaker pitfall: don't reach for 엿보다 just because English 'take a peek' sounds casual and harmless — in Korean the literal verb implies secrecy and intrusion, so for an innocent quick glance use 살짝 보다 or 힐끔 보다 instead.

usage: to glare with eyes wide open
눈을 부릅뜨다 intensifies the fierce stare
Casual near-synonym; often a quick sharp glare
to glare for a long while
한참 stretches the angry stare in time
examples: 강아지가 낯선 사람을 노려봐요
The dog is glaring at the stranger
Simple present; an animal sensing a threat
새치기한 사람을 다들 노려봤어요
Everyone glared at the person who cut in line
Common social-irritation scene; -았 past
화가 났는지 저를 한참 노려봤어요
Maybe they were angry — they glared at me for a while
-는지 = (wondering) whether; expresses hostility

A close casual synonym is 째려보다, which is more colloquial and often a quick, sharp dirty look, whereas 노려보다 can be a sustained, intense glare. Because 노리다 also means 'to covet/eye a target', 노려보다 occasionally edges toward 'eye something one is after', but its default is anger. It contracts 노려보 + -아 → 노려봐요, past 노려봤어요. English-speaker pitfall: never use 노려보다 where neutral English 'look at' would do — it always injects hostility, so for a plain look use 보다 and for an awkward stare use 쳐다보다.

usage: 쓱 captures a single swift sweep of the eyes
쭉 implies scanning top to bottom in one go
Getting an overview of the entirety
examples: 메뉴를 쓱 훑어봤어요
I gave the menu a quick once-over
쓱 훑어보다 = fast scan; -았 past
출근하면서 뉴스를 훑어봐요
I skim the news on my way to work
-면서 = while; a daily commuter habit
계약서를 훑어보지만 말고 꼼꼼히 읽으세요
Don't just skim the contract — read it carefully
Contrasts 훑어보다 (skim) with 꼼꼼히 읽다 (read closely)
nuance: 훑어보다 builds on 훑다 ('to strip/run along a surface', as in running a hand down a stalk) plus 보다, so it pictures the eyes sliding rapidly over a surface to grab the gist — skimming a menu, an article, a resume. The decisive contrast is with 살펴보다: 살펴보다 is slow, careful inspection, while 훑어보다 is a fast once-over, so 계약서를 훑어보다 (skim the contract) vs 계약서를 살펴보다 (go through it carefully) carry opposite levels of diligence. English-speaker pitfall: English 'look over' covers both skimming and scrutinizing, but 훑어보다 only means the quick-skim end — if you actually read something thoroughly, say 살펴봤어요 or 꼼꼼히 읽었어요, because 훑어봤어요 admits you only glanced.

usage: 우연히 softens it to accidental overhearing
본의 아니게 = not on purpose; defuses the blame
Classic scene of listening through a door
examples: 남의 통화를 엿들으면 안 돼요
You shouldn't listen in on someone's phone call
-면 안 되다 forbids it; note ㄷ→ㄹ in 엿들으면
카페에서 옆자리 얘기를 본의 아니게 엿들었어요
At the cafe I unintentionally overheard the next table
본의 아니게 frames it as accidental; -았 past 엿들었어요
문 앞에서 엿듣다가 들켰어요
I got caught eavesdropping at the door
엿듣다가 들키다 = get caught mid-eavesdrop; -다가 interrupts

English-speaker pitfall (two of them): first, never write 엿듣어요 — that ignores the ㄷ-irregular; it must be 엿들어요. english: to understand (by hearing) / catch what is said
usage: to fail to catch what's said
The single most useful learner phrase; 못 + ㄷ-irregular
to not catch a single word
Pairs with a request for slower speech
to catch one's drift / get the point
Idiom 말귀를 알아듣다 = understand what someone means
examples: 무슨 말인지 못 알아들었어요
I couldn't catch what you were saying
Survival line; 못 + past 알아들었어요
발음이 빨라서 하나도 못 알아들었어요
The speech was so fast I couldn't catch a thing
하나도 못 알아듣다; -아서 gives the reason
천천히 말하면 알아들을 수 있어요

-면 conditional + 알아들을 수 있다 (note ㄷ→ㄹ)

English-speaker pitfall (two): don't write 알아듣어요 — the ㄷ-irregular makes it 알아들어요; and don't substitute 이해하다 when you simply mean you caught the words, since 이해해요 claims you grasped the idea, not that you heard it.
